items.title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
items.summary: Video generation has progressed from isolated clips to coherent short-form audiovisual sequences, and the bottleneck is shifting from rendering to semantic control. This report summarizes the observations and insights on multimodal understanding gained from successive generations of Kling. We argue that generation quality is the projection of multimodal understanding through the entire data--conditioning--alignment--evaluation chain, and we examine this chain module by module. Kling-MLLM, a shared multimodal foundation model that unifies image, video, audio, synchronized audio--video, and interleaved inputs, is specialized for each downstream module. Because a DiT is trained on far fewer training samples than a language model, we treat captioning as a semantic contract that maximizes description density, and extend it to reference-grounded captioning that makes reference bindings explicit. Prompt enhancement translates user intent into this caption distribution: basic PE is derived from captions of compelling videos and refined with text-level and generator-in-the-loop reinforcement learning, while agentic PE refines the story and retrieves compelling examples. items.title: Is Forgetting Unified? Exploring Concept Unlearning in Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) integrate image generation and visual understanding, but are existing single-pathway unlearning methods sufficient to suppress target concepts across both? In this work, we study cross-pathway concept unlearning. Our goal is to prevent a model from both generating images of a target concept and identifying it in input images, while preserving other capabilities. To this end, we introduce UUBench, a diagnostic benchmark covering 30 target concepts and 60 semantically related neighboring concepts. Experiments on representative UMMs show that the evaluated single-pathway methods achieve limited joint forgetting: generation-side editors strongly suppress target generation but yield limited forgetting in visual understanding, while understanding-side baselines struggle to achieve substantial forgetting even in their own pathway. Their direct composition also yields limited joint forgetting. We therefore propose UniForget, achieving joint forgetting rates of 80.0% on BAGEL-7B-MoT and 92.7% on Janus-Pro-7B, outperforming representative baselines. Further analysis reveals trade-offs between joint forgetting and capability preservation.

items.title: ViRel-Budget: Reliability-Constrained Visual-Token Budgeting for Green Vision-Language Inference
items.summary: Visual-token pruning promises greener vision-language model (VLM) inference, but accuracy alone cannot show whether compression preserves visual reliance or produces real systems savings. We present ViRel-Budget, a reliability-constrained framework that constructs intervention-defined safety labels, learns budget-specific risk predictors without fine-tuning the VLM, and executes one selected action under a calibrated risk limit. We evaluate LLaVA-1.5-7B and 13B with FastV, SCOPE, and deterministic Random pruning using 1,200 development and 900 group-isolated prospective queries, and assess energy robustness across three independent 210-query draws. On the prospective evaluation, SCOPE satisfies the 5% risk limit with unsafe-acceptance rates of 1.67% at 7B and 2.89% at 13B. Across the separate replication draws, it reduces GPU energy by 11.87% and 10.62%, respectively. FastV and Random do not establish energy savings despite reducing tokens, showing that sparsity is not inherently green. Using paired GPU telemetry, carbon estimation, and reliability-adjusted efficiency metrics, ViRel-Budget identifies reliability-qualified configurations whose computational savings translate into defensible environmental benefits.

items.title: DATP: Training-Free Depth-Aware Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: The massive redundancy of visual tokens in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) creates a critical computational bottleneck during large language model (LLM) prefill. Recent training-free pruning methods provide plug-and-play acceleration, yet their pruning decisions often rely on limited visual states or delayed in-LLM signals, which may underexploit both the layer-wise evolution of visual representations and the query-specific relevance of local regions. We propose DATP (Depth-Aware Token Pruning), a training-free early-pruning framework that selects compact visual tokens before they enter the LLM. DATP combines two complementary signals: Depth-aware Layer Aggregation (DALA), which aggregates multi-layer visual saliency trajectories to construct a high-recall structural prior, and Cross-modal Attention Gating (CMAG), which introduces a lightweight prompt-conditioned relevance signal to suppress visually salient but task-irrelevant tokens. Experiments on LLaVA-v1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, and Qwen2.5-VL show that DATP achieves a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off under aggressive token budgets. On LLaVA-v1.5, DATP preserves 95.7% of the full-token performance while retaining only 11% of the visual tokens. Across the reported multimodal reasoning and hallucination-sensitive benchmark settings, DATP generally outperforms the evaluated training-free pruning baselines.

items.title: From Forensic Masks to Ranked Reasons: Evidence-Guided Multimodal Explanation for Document Image Tampering
items.summary: Document images, including scanned archives, contracts, certificates, and administrative records, are frequently used as digital evidence. Local edits to characters, seals, dates, or handwritten fields can change their meaning while leaving only subtle forensic traces. Existing localization models can predict suspicious regions, but their masks are difficult to interpret; general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can describe document content, but often miss low-level tampering evidence or hallucinate unsupported explanations. We present an evidence-guided multimodal framework that turns forensic localization masks into structured, ranked document tampering explanations. A localization front-end predicts a tampering probability map, which is binarized and converted into coordinate prompts. A LoRA-tuned Qwen3-VL-4B model then generates a structured response containing tampering judgment, localization, evidence-based rationales, and rationale ranking. We construct 6,000 instruction-tuning samples from archival document tampering images and DocTamper. items.title: FlowBench: Counterfactual Imagination Training for Spatial Intelligence
items.summary: Humans imagine scene changes under hypothetical motions, an ability central to spatial reasoning and robotic planning. However, this capability remains underexplored in vision-language models and world models. We formalize this capability as Counterfactual Spatial Imagination (CSI) and introduce FlowBench, a resource for training and evaluating both, with 428K training examples spanning simulated and real-world scenes, household environments and tabletop manipulation, and diverse question types. A scalable, fully automatic pipeline pairs each hypothetical motion with spatial questions and, in simulation, exact outcome frames and optical flow. For VLMs, proprietary models exhibit an imagination gap, performing worse when motion outcomes must be inferred than when observed, and open-source models perform near chance; fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B on FlowBench-Sim-Train raises its accuracy by 29.5 percentage points in simulation and 16.9 on real images, a strong sim-to-real transfer. For world models, training on FlowBench-Sim improves text-to-flow prediction for all four model families we test, raising the accuracy of Psi-0.6 from 52.1% to 61.7%. FlowBench thus serves as a training and evaluation resource for both. Code and datasets are released at https://github.com/liuyifan22/FlowBench.

An auditor uses reward predictions and uncertainty to identify overestimation patterns learned from paired imagined videos and real executions. The retained real trajectories then supervise behavior cloning. items.title: Diffusion-DRF: Free, Rich, and Differentiable Reward for Video Diffusion Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Video diffusion alignment has been heavily relied on scalar rewards. These rewards are typically derived from learned reward models in human preference datasets, requiring additional training and extensive collection. Moreover, scalar rewards provide coarse, global supervision, offering limited prompt-generation mismatch credit assignment and making models prone to reward exploitation and unstable optimization. We propose Diffusion-DRF, a free, rich, and differentiable reward framework for video diffusion fine-tuning. Diffusion-DRF employs a frozen, off-the-shelf Vision-Language Model (VLM) as the critic, eliminating the need for reward model training. Instead of relying on a single scalar reward, it decomposes each user prompt into multi-dimensional questions with freeform dense VQA explanation queries, yielding information-rich feedback. By direct differentiable optimization over this rich feedback, Diffusion-DRF achieves stable reward-based tuning without preference datasets collection. Diffusion-DRF achieves significant gains both quantitatively and qualitatively, outperforming state-of-the-art Flow-GRPO by 4.74% in overall performance on unseen VBench-2.0.

items.title: VideoZeroBench: Probing the Limits of Video MLLMs with Spatio-Temporal Evidence Verification
items.summary: Video multimodal large language models achieve strong results on existing benchmarks, but answer accuracy alone does not establish whether they can locate the evidence needed to answer a question. We introduce VideoZeroBench, a challenging long-video benchmark with manually annotated question-answer pairs spanning 13 video domains. Questions target fine-grained cues, fleeting events, and evidence distributed across multiple segments. Temporal intervals and key-frame boxes are annotated where applicable. All questions undergo two rounds of cross-verification for answer validity and evidence quality. Our five-level diagnostic protocol compares answering with and without evidence hints, then combines answer correctness with independently evaluated temporal and spatial grounding. Across 19 evaluated models, the best standard QA accuracy is 24.8% (Level-3), achieved by Gemini-3.7-Flash. No model exceeds 1.8% when correct answers and accurate spatio-temporal localization are jointly required (Level-5). Analyses of atomic abilities, evidence spans, input modalities, and thinking-with-videos inference further characterize where the evaluated systems struggle. These findings motivate more precise evidence search and localization for long-video question answering. Our code and data are publicly released.

items.title: DramaVQA: Probing Detailed Understanding of Ultra-Long TV Dramas
items.summary: Despite recent progress in long-form video understanding, current benchmarks mostly focus on short clips or hour-scale videos. This leaves a major gap in evaluating ultra-long video understanding, where videos often last tens of hours. To bridge this gap, we introduce DramaVQA, a large-scale benchmark built upon long-form TV dramas. Containing approximately 20K question-answering (QA) pairs, the scale of DramaVQA exceeds previous long-video datasets, such as Video-MME and LVBench, by an order of magnitude. Our benchmark has two main features that make it stand out from existing datasets. First, we establish a scalable, LLM-assisted annotation pipeline that uses multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to generate complex questions, followed by strict human checking to ensure high data quality. Second, DramaVQA introduces a multi-level time structure; queries are designed across different video lengths, with the hardest questions requiring overall understanding across the entire drama. Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art MLLMs face major challenges when tested on these very long videos, highlighting the need for agentic AI algorithms capable of managing long-term memory. The project is available at https://github.com/xinyuehuo/DramaVQA

items.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can listen and see, but how do audio and visual signals actually travel through the network to shape an answer? items.title: DiMuRe: Diagnosis-Guided Multilevel Recovery for Robotic Task Execution
items.summary: Disturbances can invalidate the conditions required by a robot's next action even when much of its task program remains useful. A recovery system must therefore choose a response suited to the current state. We present DiMuRe (diagnosis-guided multilevel recovery), a framework for robot-use agents that uses phase-specific evidence and method preconditions to select program reuse or predefined recovery skills, including bounded vision-language-action (VLA) grasping. After the original program exits, a multimodal large language model (MLLM) can generate corrective code from images and execution feedback. Local verification checks the outcome of each recovery attempt. We also introduce LIBERO-Disturb, a benchmark for robustness and recovery under mid-execution disturbances, supporting program-based agents and VLA policies. On 801 scheduled disturbed Encore development cases, Local DiMuRe (program reuse and recovery skills) achieves 77.65% complete-task success, compared with 58.68% for the original program under the same physical-step allowance. Full DiMuRe achieves 81.90% with terminal replanning, an additional step allowance, and early handoff. Local DiMuRe also uses fewer physical steps per scheduled episode than the original program.

items.title: Explainable Diabetic Retinopathy Classification Using Vision Foundation Models
items.summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable blindness, and automated screening must be both accurate and trustworthy. We study an explainable DR classification framework built on vision foundation models and three transfer learning strategies. Three backbones, DINOv2, CLIP, and Vision Transformer (ViT), were adapted by full fine-tuning, linear probing, and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). Models were trained and internally evaluated on the ODIR dataset and externally evaluated on APTOS to assess generalization. DINOv2-LoRA achieved the highest internal AUROC (0.758), whereas DINOv2 and ViT full fine-tuning achieved the highest external AUROC (0.920). Probability calibration was assessed with reliability analysis after isotonic regression. For explainability, Grad-CAM and HiResCAM maps were compared with expert-annotated lesion masks from the IDRiD dataset using Dice, Intersection over Union (IoU), and Pointing Game metrics. The results show that foundation models, particularly DINOv2, provide strong predictive performance, and that LoRA is a parameter-efficient alternative to full fine-tuning. Spatial overlap between explanation maps and annotated lesions was limited (mean Dice of about 0.13 for the combined lesion mask), which highlights the value of quantitatively testing whether model attention corresponds to clinically relevant retinal lesions.

items.title: CLAP: Direct VLM-to-VLA Adaptation via Language-Action Grounding
items.summary: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) inherit semantic capabilities from pretrained VLMs, yet large-scale post-training on robot data and architectural modifications can reshape the backbone so extensively that it becomes difficult to isolate what the VLM contributes to control. items.title: BtsPruner: Role-Aware Visual Token Pruning for Large Vision-Language Models

items.title: Bidirectional Centered Score Matching for Discrete Diffusion Distillation
items.summary: Discrete diffusion models with parallel decoding are often distilled using token-wise KL objectives. Although token-wise KL exactly matches the corresponding product-form block distributions, its probability-space optimization geometry and teacher-only candidate truncation may provide insufficient supervision under aggressive few-step distillation. Concrete Score Matching (CSM) provides an alternative within-position objective by aligning relative logit geometry, but its complete pairwise form incurs $\mathcal{O}(|\mathcal{V}|^2)$ complexity. We propose Bidirectional Centered Score Matching (BCSM), an efficient within-position distillation objective that constructs an $\mathcal{O}(K)$ bidirectional active set, reduces pairwise comparisons to $\mathcal{O}(K^2)$, and factorizes them into an $\mathcal{O}(K)$ objective. We further introduce cross-timestep transition alignment. Experiments demonstrate strong quality--efficiency trade-offs, including up to $6\times$ NFE reduction with a 16.9\% relative HumanEval gain and a 15.1\% relative MMMU gain at single-step inference.

items.title: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements

items.title: Therapy-FIS: A Dataset for Assessing Facilitative Interpersonal Skills in Psychotherapeutic Setting
items.summary: Facilitative Interpersonal Skills (FIS) is a performance-based assessment method that provides a structured framework for evaluating the interpersonal competencies of mental health professionals. However, existing FIS assessment relies heavily on human observer ratings, making the evaluation process labor-intensive, costly, and difficult to scale. Progress toward automated FIS assessment has also been constrained by the lack of publicly available professional data in psychotherapy settings. To address this limitation, we introduce Therapy-FIS, a dataset for automated FIS assessment in standardized psychotherapy tasks. To our knowledge, Therapy-FIS is the first publicly available dataset in this domain. It contains facial, acoustic, and textual signals derived from standardized therapist responses to standardized mock patient stimulus clips, based on 890 therapist video recordings and 8 patient videos, and is rated with eight FIS subscale ratings and an overall FIS score. Built on Therapy-FIS, we further establish a benchmark with two downstream tasks: Therapist Performance Rating and Joint Therapist--mock-Patient Performance Rating. items.title: CurEvo: Curriculum-Guided Self-Evolution for Video Understanding
items.summary: Recent self-evolution frameworks for video understanding have demonstrated the potential for autonomous improvement from unlabeled videos. However, existing approaches often suffer from weakly controlled optimization and capability progression because they lack structured guidance for generating, evaluating, and reusing supervision throughout the iterative learning process. We present CurEvo, a curriculum-guided self-evolution framework that organizes this loop as a competence-aware progression. Curriculum-Guided Self-Evolution maintains a competence-aware curriculum state and cumulative training pool across iterations. Within this loop, Multi-Dimensional Question Generation supplies complementary supervision, from directly verifiable structural questions for perception to type-conditioned questions for recognition and understanding. Type-Adaptive Evaluation separately assesses question quality and answer reliability with criteria matched to each type's evidence; its scores determine which pairs enter the pool and how the next curriculum state is updated. Across seven backbones and four VideoQA benchmarks, CurEvo consistently improves benchmark accuracy and benchmark semantic score. items.title: ELMA: Benchmarking Anaphoric Compositions for Long-Term Text-to-Motion Generation
items.summary: Text-guided long-term human motion generation is essential for applications such as continuously operating digital avatars. Despite recent progress on short clips, existing models struggle with multi-segment instructions that involve anaphora, where constraints established in earlier segments must be preserved over time. In this paper, we introduce a novel task of long-term motion generation from such anaphoric compositions. To address this gap, we present ELMA, an episodic long-term motion dataset with dense segment-level annotations that preserve cross-segment dependencies. Built via a fully automated collection and filtering pipeline, ELMA extracts high-quality, continuous 30-second clips from in-the-wild videos, capturing the episodic narratives necessary for long-range state modeling. Using ELMA, we benchmark representative long-term motion generation models under independent and anaphoric instruction settings, and study whether contextual fine-tuning improves long-range state modeling. Our extensive experiments provide insights into the capabilities and limitations of existing models in handling context-dependent instructions. These findings highlight the challenge of modeling cross-segment dependencies and offer valuable directions for developing more coherent and semantically consistent long-term motion generation models.

items.title: PACE: Phase-Aware Chunk Execution for Robot Policies with Action Chunking
items.summary: Action-chunking robot policies predict sequences of future actions, but deployment requires choosing how many actions to execute before replanning. The execution horizon trades off feedback frequency against motion continuity. However, success varies non-monotonically with the execution horizon, and the best-performing horizon differs across tasks. These effects make a single fixed horizon unreliable as a default execution strategy across tasks. We propose PACE (Phase-Aware Chunk Execution), a training-free method that selects execution horizons online from predicted action chunks. PACE uses prominent low-speed valleys in the predicted speed profile as candidate replanning boundaries, exploiting the phase-dependent kinematics of manipulation trajectories. By default, PACE calibrates the valley threshold from each task's existing training demonstrations, without task-specific fixed-horizon tuning. On the 50-task RoboTwin2.0 benchmark, PACE improves average success from 57.8% to 64.2% over the strongest fixed-horizon baseline and outperforms the adaptive execution baselines AAC and AutoHorizon. items.title: SONIC-K1: Porting a Universal Humanoid Motion Tracker to a Small Humanoid on a Single GPU
items.summary: We present SONIC-K1, to our knowledge the first open-weights whole-body motion tracker for the Booster K1 humanoid, obtained by adapting the SONIC framework to this smaller robot. The policy is trained from scratch on a single shared GPU with a small fraction of the compute reported for SONIC. In MuJoCo simulation, it tracks nearly all held-out motion clips and performs well on external benchmarks under SONIC's success criterion. On the real K1, it tracks upper-body and slow motions, while stepping and turning remain less reliable, and simulation experiments show a sensitivity to action latency. These results show broad motion-tracking capability on a modest training budget and point to quantitative hardware evaluation as the main next step. Code, policy weights and evaluation tools are publicly available.

items.title: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use

items.title: Semantic-GSL: Vision-Language Semantics for Information-Theoretic Gas Source Localization
items.summary: This study presents Semantic-GSL, a semantic-informed vision-integrated framework for gas source localization (GSL) in unknown indoor environments. Indoor GSL is challenging because gas concentration measurements are sparse and noisy, while airflow often deviates from simplified dispersion models. Existing vision-integrated approaches rely on predefined object categories or large multimodal models that are impractical for on-board deployment. To address these limitations, we employ a lightweight two-stage vision-language model framework combining Grounding DINO and CLIP for open-set detection of gas-related objects using general environmental descriptions. The extracted semantic information is probabilistically incorporated into posterior estimation through the proposed semantic-informed particle filter, yielding a semantically informative posterior that enables efficient information-theoretic source search. Simulations demonstrate enhanced search efficiency and robust localization across diverse environments, while real-world experiments confirm the feasibility of on-board deployment.

items.title: Running a 20B Video Diffusion Transformer on Consumer Hardware: A Deployment and Measurement Report for MiniMax H3 on Apple Silicon

items.title: VLMs Read Aloud: The Gap Between Recognizing and Using Visual Text
items.summary: Visual-text compression renders long contexts as images and is engineered around how much of the text a vision-language model (VLM) can recover. Yet recovered text is not usable text. Putting the evidence into words closes it: thinking VLMs recite the evidence in their thinking, and their own transcript, written without seeing the question, recovers most of what thinking adds. items.summary: Foundational vision models have become the de facto standard for many vision tasks due to their strong performance. However, they are notoriously opaque and remain hard to interpret. items.summary: Previous research shows that vision-language (VL) models struggle to understand fine-grained image details and tend to focus on the overall layout. Moreover, any weakness in English tends to be further amplified in the multilingual setting. To study that, we extend InpaintCOCO, an English dataset focused on fine-grained visual details, to 13 typologically diverse languages across five language families, creating MultiInpaintCOCO - a new multilingual benchmark of 953 minimal-pair examples. We further test several state-of-the-art models in multilingual multimodal retrieval, considering both light VL CLIP-like encoders and large language models. Our results show that performance degrades substantially for lower-resource languages, with the strongest predictor being the data resources available for the languages rather than typological similarity to English. In cross-lingual retrieval, most models exhibit a systematic bias toward English: when given a correct caption in a non-English language and an incorrect one in English, models preferentially select the English caption. This bias varies considerably across architectures. items.title: OSGR: Observation-Support Graph Reasoning for Earth Observation Question Answering
items.summary: Answering geographic queries over Earth observation (EO) archives requires solving a joint retrieval-and-derivation problem under strict spatiotemporal constraints. Existing LLM agents fail to ground observation items or suffer from search-space explosion. We propose OSGR, a two-stage framework that factorizes this search into offline symbolic concept deduction and online Relation-Conditioned Grounding. OSGR leverages an offline Observation-Support Graph to deduce valid target-to-result support paths at the concept level, and applies spatiotemporal compatibility kernels to instantiate grounded observation-item sets. On Earth-Bench and DisasterM3-Reason, OSGR improves GPT-4o accuracy from 49.3\% to 63.7\% while reducing the execution-step ratio from 2.9 to 2.5.

items.summary: Foundation models are becoming remarkably reliable at high-level reasoning, yet they remain too slow and costly to serve as fine-grained controllers. items.title: EdgeCurator: Efficient Cross-Modal Grounding for Real-Time Language-Guided UAV Navigation
items.summary: Deploying cross-modal representations on a micro Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) requires accurate language–vision alignment and low-latency inference under tight compute constraints. Heavy Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide strong semantic reasoning but are often unsuitable for an onboard control loop, whereas lightweight visual backbones commonly defer language fusion to a separate planning stage. We present EdgeCurator, a compact end-to-end early-fusion framework for real-time language-guided UAV navigation in access-controlled indoor spaces. Its Semantic-Spatial Grounding (SSG) Head converts lightweight text embeddings into semantic queries and uses conditioned deformable cross-attention to sparsely sample multi-scale visual features. On the custom Expo-VLN benchmark, EdgeCurator uses 14.8M parameters, runs at 54 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, and reaches 67.3% grounding accuracy and 62.8% navigation success. We additionally report 60 controlled physical trials with two target types, achieving 78.3% success. These trials test onboard Sim2Real feasibility for pre-opening inspection and curation assistance; they do not establish operation around visitors or generalization to full exhibition deployments. The results position EdgeCurator as an efficiency-oriented cross-modal representation and grounding system for resource-constrained aerial agents.

items.title: Lance: A LANGUAGE-ANCHORED CLOSED-LOOP ESTIMATOR for Bridging Low-Level Image Fusion and High-Level Semantic Understanding in Remote Sensing
items.summary: Remote sensing image fusion and semantic interpretation are usually optimized separately, so reconstruction quality need not preserve downstream retrieval utility. We propose LANCE, which uses structured language as an explicit, indexable semantic state. A frozen vision–language model maps the input to a closed-vocabulary text record; a language-conditioned generator fuses the imagery; and a dense verifier with a differentiable continuous summarizer re-describes the output. Text–text consistency and anti-collapse contrastive text–mask losses with negative queries close the loop without dense annotations or VLM fine-tuning. A variational EM formulation yields a per-step contraction result under regularity assumptions, distinguishing semantic faithfulness from verifier overfitting. Across seven test sets on GF2, QuickBird, WorldView-III, and WorldView-II, LANCE improves reduced-scale reference metrics by up to 11.7% (median 2.1%) over the strongest learning baseline. Independent evaluation using a held-out VLM and a supervised aerial detector yields gains of +6.4 mAP and +0.072 open-vocabulary F1 over the closest competitor. Text perturbations, cross-verifier transfer, and pseudo-RGB ablations examine the mechanisms underlying these gains. The framework connects image fusion to verifiable semantic representations for multimodal retrieval and knowledge management.

items.title: VidUEU-Agent: A Data-Curation Agent for Multimodal Understanding, Editing, and Unified Tasks
items.summary: The advancement of multimodal learning is heavily constrained by the scarcity and high annotation cost of high-quality instruction data. While raw videos offer an abundant and dynamic source of visual knowledge, transforming them into precise instruction data remains highly challenging. To bridge this gap, we present VidUEU-Agent, an automated pipeline that synthesizes instruction data from raw videos for multimodal understanding, editing, and unified tasks. VidUEU-Agent follows a four-stage pipeline: it performs global perception to filter low-quality shots, mines keyframes and multimodal signals, constructs metadata and routes the metadata to synthesize instruction samples. More importantly, our agent framework can autonomously iterate the data distribution based on downstream training results, thereby optimizing data quality, balance, and training effectiveness. Scaling this pipeline, we construct VidUEU-100K, a large-scale dataset of 100K training samples spanning multiple domains and tasks, providing a robust foundation for developing comprehensive multimodal capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that fine-tuning baseline models on VidUEU-100K yields significant and consistent performance gains across diverse representative benchmarks, validating the effectiveness of our proposed agent framework and dataset.

items.title: VISRA: Vision-Language Induced Supervision and Representation Alignment for Long-Tailed Generalized Category Discovery
items.summary: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) aims to classify unlabeled data containing both known and novel classes, given only labels for known classes. Existing GCD methods typically assume a relatively balanced data distribution, an assumption that breaks down in realistic open-world scenarios. In this paper, we study Long-Tailed Generalized Category Discovery (LT-GCD), where both labeled and unlabeled data follow long-tailed distributions. Under such conditions, training signals are dominated by known categories; this imbalance biases representation learning and weakens novel-category discovery. To address these challenges, we propose VISRA, a semantic-driven framework for LT-GCD built upon a parametric GCD pipeline. Rather than relying solely on distribution debiasing, our framework leverages Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to provide additional semantic supervision for representative novel-class instances and guide visual representation learning. Experimental results on three long-tailed datasets demonstrate that VISRA achieves state-of-the-art performance, effectively alleviating novel-class supervision deficiency and learning more discriminative representations under severe imbalance. Our code and prompt are available at https://github.com/EileanZYZ/VISRA.

items.summary: Interoperability between building information modeling (BIM) platforms remains a significant challenge despite standardization efforts. This paper presents a controlled benchmark study of material data retention in Revit–ArchiCAD conversions via the Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) standard using three representative models (house, hotel, hospital). Material, geometric, and parametric attributes are compared to pre- and postconversion with automated scripts and commercial viewers. We find persistent material losses, even with exchange add-ins with complex models degrading the most; losses concentrate on customs and regulatory attributes (e.g., fire/thermal properties). We discuss limitations of current automation and IFC implementations and recommend workflow, schema, and tool improvements for mitigation. Looking forward, we introduce vision-language models (VLMs) as a complementary, image-grounded verification layer that can surface visually evident material changes and align them with IFC properties, pointing toward semiautomated, real-time auditing of BIM interoperability.

items.title: GQA-Q2Q: A Large-scale Benchmark for Entity Ambiguity Resolution in Visual Question Answering
items.summary: Vision-language models achieve remarkable results on various visual question-answering benchmarks. However, they struggle with ambiguous questions where the target entity is unclear. items.title: What Remains in Sight? Autoregressive Video Decoding as Representation-Guided Context Rewriting
items.summary: Long-horizon video generation is increasingly moving toward autoregressive rollout, where each newly generated segment becomes part of the evidence used for future prediction. At each step, \textsc{ReCR} builds a selected visible context from the generated history by using internal decoder representations to favor context units that match the global rollout state, avoid redundancy with the recent continuation, preserve temporal boundary coverage, and widen the range of spatial layouts in view. items.title: FloMo: 3D Scene Flow as a World Action Model Intermediate for Learning from Human Video

items.title: More Accurate, Less Human: Gestalt Grouping in Vision Models
items.summary: Human vision organizes what it sees into wholes: same-colored points group into series, similar marks cohere into categories, and shapes complete into recognizable objects. These are the Gestalt operations that visualization design builds on. Whether vision models organize visual content this way has not been systematically tested. We introduce a behavioral battery that scores models against human data from prior perception studies on four grouping tasks: mark-color odd-one-out, color-series counting, silhouette recognition, and object odd-one-out. The battery reveals that agreement with human responses captures aspects of perceptual organization that conventional performance metrics fail to distinguish, with several closed models exhibiting substantially lower alignment than their benchmark accuracy would suggest. Scoring against published perception data therefore gives visualization research a reusable yardstick, requiring no new user study, for auditing whether the models now entering visualization pipelines organize what they see the way their human audience does.

items.summary: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) aims to retrieve a target image given a reference image and a modification text. Although recent approaches leveraging Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown significant progress, we argue that the MLLM's compositional understanding remains underutilized. This stems from directly mapping composed queries into a retrieval embedding via contrastive supervision alone, without explicitly resolving the intended visual modifications. In this work, we introduce Factorized MLLM Embeddings (FactEmbed), which decouples compositional query comprehension from building discriminative embeddings. Rather than directly projecting the composed query into a single embedding without internal reasoning, FactEmbed employs a set of factorized latents that simulate the intended visual modifications via an intermediate target imagination objective. This process encourages the latents to ground into target semantics before forming discriminative representations for retrieval. Subsequently, to propagate these factorized representations throughout the model for retrieval, we optimize a factor-level contrastive loss while distilling the decomposed representations into a deeper attention layer of the MLLM. items.title: Asynchronous Robot Policies
items.summary: Scaling vision-language foundation models has significantly advanced generalist robot manipulation, but the increased model scale introduces computational latency that degrades real-time physical reactivity. Existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) architectures execute high-level semantic reasoning and action ex- ecution sequentially within the primary control loop, creating a fundamental tension between semantic-reasoning capability and robot agility. To address this, we propose Asynchronous Robot Policy (ARP), an architectural framework that decouples semantic reasoning from low-level action generation using asynchronous processes operating at independent frequencies. In ARP, a high-capacity Vision-Language Model (VLM) asynchronously updates a semantic memory at low fre- quency, while a lightweight Vision-Action Expert, conditioned on this semantic memory, generates robot actions at a much higher control frequency. Such a formulation, enables having a fast perception-action loop without compromising on the semantic capability. To overcome asynchronous memory staleness, ARP trains the vision-action expert on the semantic staleness and execution delay, with temporally mismatched observation across processes. items.title: PGuard: A Native, Streaming, and Plug-in Guardrail for Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: As streaming generation becomes the dominant serving paradigm for both text-only and multimodal large language models, ensuring safety throughout the generation process has become a critical challenge. We introduce PGuard, a native, streaming, and plug-in guardrail that transforms safety monitoring from an external serving dependency into an integrated capability of the backbone model. PGuard directly leverages the backbone's intermediate representations for token-level safety detection, without altering its original inference pathway or generation behavior. Specifically, dynamic layer gating selectively aggregates residual-stream representations across layers to extract safety-relevant signals during both prefill and autoregressive decoding. To balance detection accuracy and computational efficiency, PGuard supports multiple representation-modeling architectures, including a lightweight stateless variant and sequence-aware variants built on multi-scale causal EMA-attention and GRU-based recurrent modules. Its design also accounts for the execution characteristics of LLM serving frameworks, such as SGLang, optimizing computation and data access to minimize additional runtime and synchronization overhead. items.title: LLM Meets Traffic: Traffic-Aware Large Language Models for Next POI Recommendation in Vehicle Navigation Interfaces
items.summary: Next Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation is a production-relevant task for modern in-car navigation interfaces. Given a user's current and historical context, the system can suggest the next destination while accounting for both user preference and travel feasibility. However, existing Large Language Models (LLMs) for next POI recommendation (1) overlook real-time traffic conditions and thus fail to account for user-specific trade-offs between POI preferences and travel time, and (2) rely on text embedding-based POI candidate retrieval, which may surface semantically similar yet geographically implausible POIs. To address these limitations, we propose TraPOI, a Traffic-aware LLM for Next POI Recommendation. TraPOI consists of (i) a multimodal embedding alignment module to project POI, GPS, and traffic data into the LLM's latent space, and (ii) a multi-view candidate retrieval module that retrieves distance-based and embedding-based candidates to facilitate spatially feasible and semantically relevant next POI recommendation. We also introduce (iii) multimodal prompting to explicitly incorporate traffic and spatial context into the LLM's reasoning process. We constructed two novel datasets aligning check-in records with real-time traffic data from Seoul and California (CA) to validate our approach. items.title: Reviso: Not All Visual Evidence Deserves Equal Attention in Video Captioning
items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate detailed video captions, yet they may overemphasize minor details while overlooking essential context and key events. We argue that not all visual evidence deserves equal attention, as the importance of visual information depends on the content of each video. Motivated by this observation, we propose Reviso, an agentic video captioning framework that learns what to observe and how to gather relevant visual evidence. From a low-frame-rate global preview, Reviso constructs a hierarchical Context--Focus--Points (CFP) observation plan that identifies the video context, prioritizes key aspects, and defines concrete observation targets and corresponding tools. Guided by this plan, Reviso performs goal-directed active perception by selectively revisiting temporal segments and combining tools for fine-grained inspection. It interprets the acquired evidence, updates its plan as needed, and integrates global and local information to generate the final caption. To learn this observation strategy, we develop a verification-guided pipeline that constructs high-quality training trajectories through factual verification and teacher-guided refinement. items.title: Heads That Write, Not Just Point: Image Retrieval Heads in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) can process interleaved text and multiple images in a single context, but how they internally identify the image relevant to a question remains poorly understood. We study this grounding step as in-context image retrieval and introduce ICIR-MCQ, a controlled probe for head-level analysis of image retrieval. Using each head's attention mass over image-token spans, we first identify sparse pointer heads that reliably point to the target image. These heads transfer beyond the probe: a single pointer head is competitive with external vision-language retrievers on a naturalistic multi-image retrieval benchmark, showing that LVLMs contain a strong internal image retrieval signal. Attention alone, however, shows where a head reads from, not what its output passes on to later layers, so we introduce a complementary output-side analysis. For each head, we train a lightweight image retriever on its value-weighted output and use it to identify writer heads, whose outputs contain enough information to identify the target image. items.title: Say the Same, Act Differently: Diagnosing and Steering Text-Action Divergence in Reasoning VLAs
items.summary: Reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) models pair physical control with natural-language rationales that supervisors can read to monitor embodied safety. Prior attacks on VLA reasoning corrupt the rationale itself and leave visible evidence in the text. We show that visual perturbations can instead alter the physical action while keeping the generated rationale word-for-word identical. At the shared text/action interface of Alpamayo for driving and InstructVLA for manipulation, our text-neutral action-subspace (TNAS) diagnostic shows that the locally most action-sensitive direction is nearly orthogonal to the active text-loss gradients, with 1.87% and 5.28% norm overlap. At equal hidden-state perturbation norms across both models, interventions along this text-neutral residual shift actions 4.64x to 47.8x more than text-gradient perturbations, whereas text-gradient perturbations induce 21.2x to 277x more text drift. Steering visual perturbations along this direction reaches the same decoupling from the image.
